subject: Migration source mapping & hosting recommendation
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: James Park <j.park@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: mapping your migration sources to deployment options

Hi James —

Great to meet today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have a clear path forward while you evaluate hosting options: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC. I pulled together the notes we discussed during the call.

Summary of your current sources (as discussed):
- Current production calls: OpenAI API (GPT-family) serving consumer-facing chat experiences (~120 QPS peak, 35M tokens/month).
- Internal research cluster: self-hosted models on legacy GPU farm (mostly FP16 floats, homegrown orchestration).
- New ML infra team: evaluating transition to a private VPC for regulated PII use cases.

Redwood recommendation (short):
- Short term (0-3 months): Move front-line low-latency chat traffic to Redwood Hosted API to reduce token cost variability and get instant SLA + streaming.
- Mid term (3-9 months): Reserve Dedicated capacity for steady throughput (disable noisy neighbor risk from public clouds) and enable autoscale bursts for holiday traffic spikes.
- Sensitive/regulatory paths: Private VPC deployment for PII pipelines and audit-controlled workflows — should be treated as a separate routing policy (we can set automatic fallbacks to Dedicated/Hosted for non-sensitive requests).

Attachments: I attached a short Dedicated QuickStart (config + sizing guidance) and a draft Mutual Action Plan with milestones for migration sprints.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm whether you want an initial proof-of-concept on Hosted API (fastest) or a Dedicated evaluation (predictable throughput).
2) Share any compliance or procurement windows (dates) so we can align the Mutual Action Plan.
3) If you need SOC2 evidence now, flag and I will loop in our security team.

Would you be open to a 30-minute follow-up on Wednesday to lock in POC vs Dedicated sizing?

Thanks,

— Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_QuickStart.pdf (8 pages), ACME_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (stub)

From: James Park <j.park@acme-retail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: ml-platform@acme-retail.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: mapping your migration sources to deployment options

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying points from our side: 

1) Timeline: Procurement wants a recommended path before the end of Q2. We can run a POC in April.
2) Migration sources: The majority of production traffic still goes to the OpenAI endpoints. Our internal team is keeping the legacy cluster for custom ops and some private models. We are evaluating a full cutover but want the ability to route certain model calls to our on-prem cluster for cost reasons.
3) Compliance: We need SOC2 artifacts and a short description of what 'Private VPC' would look like (network flow, data residency, KMS).

Question: For the scenario where we keep the legacy cluster for heavy batch workloads, how does Redwood handle hybrid routing? Can we route by model tag or customer ID?

If you can answer the routing question and share SOC2 summary, we can move to procurement review.

— James
Head of ML Platform, Acme Retail
j.park@acme-retail.com

Quoted reply below from the demo notes: 
> On Mon, Mar 22, 2027 at 14:05, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Great to meet today. Quick recap and suggested next steps...

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: James Park <j.park@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: mapping your migration sources to deployment options

James — good questions. Short answers first: yes, hybrid routing by model tag or customer ID is supported via routing policies (we can attach rules to model aliases or request metadata). Below is a slightly more detailed mapping for your three sources and our recommended deployment match: 

- OpenAI-origin traffic (low-latency public-facing chat): Hosted API initially, then migrate to Dedicated once throughput and cost predictability requirements are locked. Benefit: near-instant onboarding, streaming, and no infra ops.
- Legacy GPU cluster (batch / custom ops): Keep for strictly custom kernels and batch workloads. Use Redwood's routing layer to send model calls tagged as 'batch' or 'legacy' to your on-prem endpoint. We support an outbound connector and secure VPN peering for Private + hybrid.
- PII-sensitive pipelines: Private VPC with KMS/HSM integration, VPC peering, and audit log forwarding. We can supply a network diagram and a minimal-secrets architecture.

On routing specifics:
- Rules are evaluated in order; you can bind by request.headers.x-acme-route or by model alias (e.g., acme/retail-gpt-1:prod).
- Fallbacks: if a private endpoint is unreachable, requests can fail closed or fallback to Dedicated/Hosted depending on the policy you pick.

I've attached our SOC2 summary and a short network sketch (see links). Neha, can you confirm the procurement checklist items and estimated lead times for Dedicated capacity?

Happy to do the 30-min POC planning session on Wednesday at 10am PT if that works.

— Soojin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_Type2_summary.pdf (3 pages)

Hi James / Procurement team —

Following Soojin's note: a few practical items from our side to help Procurement triage internal timelines and required artifacts.

Required for Dedicated/purchase order: 
- Expected committed throughput (QPS) and average token length — helps us recommend instance pools and autoscale thresholds.
- Contracting window: target start date for Dedicated capacity (we recommend allowing 4–6 weeks for procurement + capacity provisioning).
- Security: SOC2 Type II report (attached), data processing agreement (DPA) template, and the list of required IP / data flow diagrams.

If you can provide a short answers doc with the above points by Friday, we'll prepare a draft SOW and an initial capacity quote.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

- We can commit to a POC in April and have answers on expected throughput by Apr 8.
- Our security team will review the SOC2 summary; they may ask for a short tech call about KMS and audit log retention.
- For hybrid routing: yes, we will start by tagging batch workloads and expect to keep legacy cluster for at least 6 months after POC.

Let's lock the POC planning session for Apr 7 at 10am PT (Sooj in the note said 10am on Wednesday but that was the 24th — latest preferable is Apr 7). I'll send a calendar invite once procurement confirms the attendees.

Thanks — looking forward to the POC.
